decided: Both human renderers (text and markdown) surface every ungrounded-leg label the engine computes: text gains the missing Deferred.Caveats loop; markdown gains caveat/note lines for Realized.Caveats, Deferred.Caveats, and Unrealized.Notes, rendered as blockquote lines under the legs table in the existing '> ...' style. No renderer drops a label the Report struct carries.
why: engine.Compute deliberately degrades per-leg (Caveats / Notes / NotAvailableReason) instead of erroring, but a label the renderer drops is a label that never existed for the reader: an events-only backend currently renders the deferred leg as '[deterministic] none in-flight' — a plausible-looking zero with no stated reason, exactly the dishonesty ADR-0008 and the review charter forbid in the numbers Finance reads. The JSON renderer already carries everything; the human renderers must match.
cost_if_wrong: Rendering noise at worst: extra caveat lines in incident channels and postmortems. The inverse error — the status quo — misprices incidents: a deferred leg silently rendered as zero during a backlog outage understates impact in the exact artifact used for severity calls.
alternatives: Caveats column in the markdown legs table — rejected: empty for healthy reports, widens the table for every reader to serve the degraded case
Footnote references from table rows — rejected: indirection in an artifact meant to be skimmed in an incident channel
Scope docs to never promise degradation labels (status quo after workspace-qe1's wording fix) — rejected: fixes the sentence, not the dishonest zero
scope: engine/report/render.go RenderText and RenderMarkdown only; regression test drives a fully-ungrounded report through both; golden files regenerated in the same PR. No change to engine.Compute, leg structs, or the JSON renderer.
